title: Cool Down Movie Marathon
description:
Beat the heat at the library! We'll be screening some summer favorites to cool down in the Auditorium all day.


The Sandlot (1993) | PG

When Scottie Smalls moves to a new neighborhood, he manages to make friends with a group of kids who play baseball at the sandlot. Together they go on a series of funny and touching adventures. The boys run into trouble when Smalls borrows a ball from his stepdad that gets hit over a fence.


Moonrise Kingdom (2012) | PG-13

The year is 1965, and the residents of New Penzance, an island off the coast of New England, inhabit a community that seems untouched by some of the bad things going on in the rest of the world. Twelve-year-olds Sam and Suzy have fallen in love and decide to run away. But a violent storm is approaching the island, forcing a group of quirky adults to mobilize a search party and find the youths before calamity strikes.


Bend It Like Beckham (2002) | PG-13

Jess Bhamra, the daughter of a strict Indian couple in London, is not permitted to play organized soccer, even though she is 18. When Jess is playing for fun one day, her impressive skills are seen by Jules Paxton, who then convinces Jess to play for her semi-pro team. Jess uses elaborate excuses to hide her matches from her family while also dealing with her romantic feelings for her coach, Joe.

title: Simple Sitting Meditation
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We meet at 9AM unless one or more people comment wanting to meet at 8AM which is my preferred time. You’re welcome to show up any time but are encouraged to post it so we have a better idea of what to expect for that day. (Those who share the same comment for start time can simply like that comment so we see how many show up for that time without potentially cluttering the comments.)

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll follow my Florida instructor’s method for balanced clinic matches\. This will typically include quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages team clotting\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Bank of America Museums on Us Weekend: July 4-5
description:
WHAT: On the nation’s 250th anniversary, Bank of America is offering Bank of America, Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank cardholders free access to 250 cultural and civic institutions to help customers experience and engage with America’s history and culture, through an expansion of the bank’s Museums on Us program. 
WHEN: Saturday, July 4th & Sunday, July 5th 
WHERE:
Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum, 2 East 91st Street, New York, NY 10128
The Intrepid Museum, Pier 86 W 46th, New York, NY 10036
The Jewish Museum, 1109 5th Ave, New York, NY 10128 (Sundays only)
The Metropolitan Museum of Art – The Met Cloisters, 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, New York, NY 10040
The Metropolitan Museum of Art – The Met Fifth Avenue, 1000 5th Ave, New York, NY 10028
Hunterdon Art Museum, 7 Lower Center Street, Clinton, NJ 08809
Liberty Science Center, 222 Jersey City Boulevard, Jersey City, NJ 07305
Montclair Art Museum, 3 South Mountain Ave., Montclair, NJ 07042
Morris Museum, 6 Normandy Heights Road, Morristown, NJ 07960 – NOTE: The Morris Museum is closed July 4th
The Newark Museum of Art, 49 Washington Street, Newark, NJ 07102 – NOTE: The Newark Museum of Art is closed July 4th
New York Botanical Garden, 2900 Southern Blvd., Bronx, NY 10458 
In addition to providing free museum admission, BofA is continuing a longstanding partnership with the Intrepid Museum and has committed to raising $500,000 and matching those dollars for a total of $1 million in support of the museum’s mission, rooted in honoring the service and sacrifice of military personnel. 
“As people travel and gather for July 4th weekend, whether in New Jersey, New York, or beyond, we’re encouraging cardholders to take advantage of Museums on Us and celebrate the people, places and institutions that have shaped our state and nation as we celebrate our country’s history,” said Alberto Garofalo, president, Bank of America New Jersey. 
WHY: Bank of America believes the arts have a unique ability to connect people and communities and help local economies thrive. Through Museums on Us, Bank of America provides its cardholders with free access during the first full weekend of every month to artistic and cultural experiences in New Jersey at celebrated institutions ranging from art, children’s and history museums to aquariums, botanical gardens, and science centers. This is one example of how the bank strengthens the local communities it serves in, creates greater cultural understanding, and expands accessibility to the arts. 
HOW: Use the bank’s location finder tool to search for participating cultural attractions. Please check with our partners directly for current operating hours and admission guidelines. Present your Bank of America, Merrill or Bank of America Private Bank credit or debit card along with a photo ID to gain free general admission to any participating institution during the first full weekend (Saturday and Sunday) of each month. Cardholders only; guests are not eligible for free admission. Program excludes fundraising events, special exhibitions, and ticketed shows. Not to be combined with other offers. Museum participation varies.

title: Lego Robotics for Elementary Students
location: RecRoom, 1 Lackawanna Plaza, Ste. 6, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) 
LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. 
In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. 
Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. 
Kids will explore:
• Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components
• Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect)
• Testing, debugging, and iterating designs
• Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas 
Details:
• 60-minute session
• Small-group format
• No prior experience required 
Community Sponsorship:
20% of seats are reserved for community sponsorship. Families interested in sponsored spots can email info@kineticmindscreative.com
for details.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We meet at 9AM unless one or more people comment wanting to meet at 8AM which is my preferred time. You’re welcome to show up any time but are encouraged to post it so we have a better idea of what to expect for that day. (Those who share the same comment for start time can simply like that comment so we see how many show up for that time without potentially cluttering the comments.)

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll follow my Florida instructor’s method for balanced clinic matches\. This will typically include quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages team clotting\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Bushkill Watershed Weird Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this point to point hike that will feature favorite old trails and some new connections between Easton and Wind Gap PA!
This time, we will meet at the Simon Silk Mill, just off of Bushkill Drive, and shuttle with as few cars as possible up to Wind Gap.
From here, we will walk a brief section of road for a tenth of a mile to a rather new trail connection.
We'll continue through part of the wooded section of Ballas Park to the former Nazareth Branch of the Lehigh and New England Railroad, which we'll follow south.
We'll reach Jacobsburg Environmental Education Center and continue through on the rail grade, then take side trails that will lead though more uplands as well as along the Bushkill Creek. We'll pass through Henry's Woods, and then make our way to the south part of the park.
Here, we'll pick up a new trail connection somewhat recently opened to Belfast.
Depending on the status of new trail connections, we'll either follow that, or we'll continue south on another short road walk to Belfast Junction. Here'll we will pick up the rail trail south into Stockertown.
There is a missing bit through Stockertown, but it is being connected. Some of it is complete, some is not.
Regardless, we have a route that will be a bit different heading southbound anyway, which will take us past an historic church, along some back streets, on some paved development trails, and then down through meadows of Rappolt Field.
We'll turn from here along one more brief road walk to reach the former Easton and Northern rail line, and this will take us almost all the way back to Simon Silk Mill to finish the hike. Distance will be about 15 miles.
There are a couple of bar and grill places in Stockertown that we might make our lunch stop.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Pepe Santana and Grupo Inkhay: Free Live Andean Concert NEW
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
Note: This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.


	
		
			
			This is the kickoff for the Paved with Promise suitcase exhibition, which will be installed in Montclair Public Library's lobby on July 1 by the Folklife Center of Northern New Jersey.
			
		
	


Enjoy the exciting live music of Pepe Santana, an Ecuadorian-born master musician based in New York City, with Grupo Inkhay, six musicians who play over two dozen musical instruments a variety of pan-pipes known as "sikus", "antaras" or "zampoñas". They also play end-nocthed vertical flutes called kenas, transverse flutes, whistles and ocarinas as well as an array of percussion instruments. 

Santana emigrated to the United States 38 years ago after the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965 commemorated in the Paved with Promise suitcase exhibition that will be installed in Montclair Public Library's lobby on July 1 by the Folklife Center of Northern New Jersey. The Andean pan-pipes Santana brought with him from Ecuador and lent to the Folklife Center are part of the display.

Santana has shared the musical traditions of the Andes, his lifelong passion, in venues such as the Lincoln Center, Alice Tully Hall, and Carnegie Hall, among many others. His emphasis on age-old sounds and rhythms has defined him as a true spokesman of traditional Andean music. 

Co-sponsored by the Folklife Center of Northern New Jersey

title: Opening Reception for the Gran Camino (Qhapaq Ñan) Exhibition: Presented by The Consulate General of Peru
description:
Join us in the Auditorium for a reception for the Gran Camino (Qhapaq Ñan) Exhibit -  which will be on display in the 1st floor July 5-July 30.

With remarks from Gabriela Porras Alor, Consulate General of Peru.

About the Qhapaq Ñan
The Qhapaq Ñan is one of the most important human creations of the Andean world. The
formalization of this vast road system, designed to make use of the Andean landscape and its
resources, not only connected communities across different regions, but also fostered an
interactive dynamic of social, economic, cultural, technological, and ideological values. From its
inception, it functioned as a backbone that integrated the peoples of the Tawantinsuyu, the
resources of the diverse regions, and the provincial administrative centers, all monitored from
Cusco.


The Qhapaq Ñan, or Inca Road, is a unique architectural space that links the rich historical,
cultural, human, and geographical diversity of Peru across both time and territory. Since the
time of the Incas and continuing to the present day, this road has facilitated the movement of
people and become the primary route of communication and ritual exchange that unites the
peoples of the Andean world.


More than 500 years after its construction, certain stretches of the road are still used by
residents of nearby villages to travel from one place to another in order to carry out activities
related to resource production and trade, to attend school or work, and to participate in
traditional festivals and celebrations—thus preserving a living tradition along the route.
Today, the Qhapaq Ñan remains a vital part of many communities that continue to use it for
communication and to safeguard ancestral knowledge through intergenerational transmission.
For this reason, Peru—through the Ministry of Culture and the Qhapaq Ñan Project – National
Headquarters—works to study, preserve, value, and keep the shared history of this Andean
heritage alive.

title: AI Governance for Cloud Data Platforms: From Policy to Practice
description:
Cloud Data Driven
As organizations deploy AI and analytics on modern cloud data platforms, governance often remains theoretical, documents exist, but execution breaks down in production. This session focuses on how to operationalize AI governance directly within cloud data platforms so that trust, compliance, and scalability are built into everyday workflows.

The session covers practical patterns for embedding governance into data pipelines and AI workflows, including data quality controls, lineage and metadata, access governance, model oversight, and audit-ready evidence. Attendees will learn why governance fails at scale, how to avoid common pitfalls, and how to align DataOps and MLOps practices to support reliable analytics and AI in the cloud.

This talk is framework-driven, vendor-neutral, and grounded in real-world challenges faced by teams running analytics and AI on cloud platforms.

description:

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

description:
Experience the spirit of France in Montclair with a joyful weekend of film, shopping, music, food, and community celebrations for all ages! 
Celebrated every year on July 14 in France and around the world, Bastille Day is France’s national holiday and a vibrant celebration of culture, community, and joie de vivre. 
In Montclair, the festivities begin Friday evening, July 10, with the annual Bastille Day Garden Party, a beloved Montclair tradition since 2008, held for the first time at the beautiful Kip’s Castle. Guests will enjoy a a cocktail reception, a refined French country buffet by Cuisine Boulud, founded by renowned four Michelin star chef Daniel Boulud, desserts created by Montclair-based pastry chef Janelle Manning, wine and cheese, live jazzy music, dancing, French-themed raffle prizes, and breathtaking views of the New York City skyline along with the chance to win two Air France tickets from New York to Paris. 
On Saturday, July 11, discover the second edition of Montclair French Shopping Day, Developed in partnership with the Montclair BID. Downtown Montclair will come alive with a French-inspired passport experience featuring shopping, tastings, special promotions, music, photo opportunities, and activities at participating businesses. Guests who complete their passports will be entered into a raffle featuring prizes from local businesses, along with entry into a grand-prize drawing for a hotel stay in France 
The celebration continues Saturday evening with a special screening of Leave One Day (Partir un jour) by Amélie Bonnin at the Clairidge Theater, presented in partnership with Montclair Film. The event will also launch a new benefit for L’Alliance New York members in Montclair: complimentary access to select French-language films at the Clairidge or Bellevue Theatre. 
Join us for a festive weekend celebrating French culture and the many ways L’Alliance enriches community life through culture, education, partnerships, and events in Montclair and beyond! 
We’ll show you why L’Alliance is French for joie de vivre.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We meet at 9AM unless one or more people comment wanting to meet at 8AM which is my preferred time. You’re welcome to show up any time but are encouraged to post it so we have a better idea of what to expect for that day. (Those who share the same comment for start time can simply like that comment so we see how many show up for that time without potentially cluttering the comments.)

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll follow my Florida instructor’s method for balanced clinic matches\. This will typically include quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages team clotting\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Los Toritos de Pucará: Peruvian Craft Painting Workshop (Children ages 5  and Adults)
location: Montclair Main - Children's Floor, Montclair Main - Green Room
description:
The Consulate General of Peru in Paterson offers a Torito de Pucará painting workshop for both adults and children. Through this activity, participants learn about the cultural significance of the Torito de Pucará while enjoying a relaxed and creative painting experience. Participants will take home their own painted Torito at the end of the workshop. Registration recommended.

 

About the Toritos de Pucará

The Toritos de Pucará are an iconic Peruvian craft originating from the town of Pucará, in the Puno region. These ceramic figures, which depict bulls adorned with vibrant colors and intricate patterns, have roots that trace back to pre-Hispanic times, influenced by the Pucará culture, which flourished between 500 B.C. and 200 A.D. in Peru’s highland region. The significance of the Toritos de Pucará is deeply connected to protection, prosperity, and fertility. Traditionally, they are placed on the rooftops of homes as amulets to attract good luck, abundant harvests, and protection for the family and household. The bull, a strong and resilient animal, is seen as a guardian that wards off negative energies and draws in abundance. Over time, and following the arrival of the Spanish, the Toritos de Pucará were incorporated into Christian beliefs, where the figure of the bull came to symbolize sacrifice and spiritual strength. In this way, these figures became a cultural icon of the Andean region, representing a syncretism between ancient agricultural traditions and new religious influences.

title: Opera--Mozart's Il Don Giovanni (Da Ponte's 1826 edition)
location: Alexander Kasser Theater, Montclair State University, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Celebrate 200 years of Italian Opera in America — Mozart’s “Don Giovanni” was the first opera ever to become a permanent part of the international repertory, from its premiere in 1787 to the present day. It was also the earliest work included in North America’s first season of Italian opera two hundred years ago–a production personally supervised and edited by Lorenzo da Ponte, the original author of the text. Teatro Nuovo is restoring the form of the title he and Mozart used, Il Don Giovanni, and is taking the anniversary occasion to restore as well everything we can learn about the performance style of the work’s early life. It presents the famous drama in a streamlined, brilliantly vivacious guise. Ricardo José Rivera, the baritone star of Teatro Nuovo’s last three seasons and more recently of the Metropolitan Opera’s I Puritani, returns in his first-ever portrayal of the Don; Geoffrey Loff leads the company’s celebrated original-instrument orchestra. The projected English titles come to us from Da Ponte’s son Luigi, created for the printed 1826 libretto. Expect the unexpected! 
Teatro Nuovo presents Bel Canto classics and rarities with a period-instrument orchestra and a performing style the Wall Street Journal calls “transformative.” For more details, visit TeatroNuovo.org 
Pre-opera Serenade at 1:30pm: The Great Garcías (I). Music by three members of the amazing family that brought Bel Canto opera to the New World: Manuel García and his daughters Maria Malibran and Pauline Viardot. Presented by Teatro Nuovo’s Resident Artist Program (Timothy Cheung, Director). 
Pre-opera Lecture at 2:00pm: Will Crutchfield introduces “Il Don Giovanni”

title: Brandywine Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this point to point hike, the next in our series of both the Brandywine Trail and the New Holland Branch of the Pennsylvania Railroad.
We meet at Sugar's Bridge Nature Area south of Downingtown Pennsylvania at 9, and shuttle with as few vehicles as possible north to our start point.
We'll begin in Marsh Creek State Park at a point we finished a previous hike in this series.
The very beginning will be field edge trails and such in a newer preserved section. From here, we will make our way east on a very brief road walk to get to where we last left off on the Brandywine Trail.
We'll pass along the Marsh Creek Lake on this trail, as well as through woods and farmlands heading to the south.
We eventually pass by the dam at Marsh Creek and descend to the Struble Trail, where we pick up the former New Holland Branch of the Pennsylvania Railroad. The Brandywine Trail follows this to Downingtown along the scenic creek.
We continue south and leave the rail bed in Downingtown, then continue on the creek.
The pleasant trail ascends through woods after another very brief road bit, and descends again to reach the Brandywine Meadows. From here to the end, we follow an old trolley bed along the creek.
This promises to be a great hike, and mostly pretty easy terrain.
We will pass places for food in Downingtown.
Distance will be about 15 miles. If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Opera--Rossini's Il Turco In Italia
location: Alexander Kasser Theater, Montclair State University, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Celebrate 200 years of Italian opera in America — Rossini’s “Il Turco in Italia” is a madcap comedy with a touch of the surreal. A poet needs a story, fast, for the opera he must write, and manipulates a colorful cast of characters to make it happen: a flirtatious heroine who has a husband, a lover-boy, and a visiting Turkish Bey all wrapped around her little finger (until she doesn’t). Teatro Nuovo favorites Vincent Graña and Mattia Venni return, joined by debut artists Kresley Figueroa and Max Alexander Cook; Elisa Citterio and Derrick Goff lead the 19th-century period-instrument orchestra on violin and cembalo. 
Pre-opera Serenade at 1:30pm: The Great Garcías (II): The adventure of bringing opera to the New World was bold and sometimes dangerous (think bandits in a remote Mexican mountain pass). Teatro Nuovo’s Resident Artists tell the story in music, letters, memoirs, and reviews. 
Pre-opera Lecture at 2:00pm: Will Crutchfield introduces “Il Turco in Italia” 
Teatro Nuovo presents Bel Canto classics and rarities with a period-instrument orchestra and a performing style the Wall Street Journal calls “transformative.” For more details, visit TeatroNuovo.org

title: Hike with Dr. Kirk! 3-4 miles
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**Tuesday, July 14, 5:30-8pm.**

Wineberry Hike after work. About 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with a long climb from the Rahway River back to the summit of South Mountain, finishing before sundown. Includes a discussion of the ecology of the Rahway River and its watershed, including the Reservation, and how the River serves as the drinking water supply. As for the wineberry, it is a non-native, invasive plant that is very common in local natural areas, including the Reservation. On the plus side, it produces a berry that looks and tastes like a raspberry and typically ripens around this date. We will stop along the way to pick and eat. Hiking poles recommended as are long pants to deter ticks. Bring plenty of water. Steady rain cancels.

Leader: Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway River Watershed Association (RRWA) and expert on local watershed issues.

Meet at: The gazebo by the dog park along Crest Drive in Maplewood.

description:

Paper quilling arrived in India as a modernized handicraft in the late 20th centuries. Indian artisans quickly embraced the medium, pairing the technique with the country's rich history of paper-making and making it their own. description:
A virtual, lively, and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio. 


Julia Strayer and Liz Maccarone will lead a lively and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio.

This is a virtual program that takes place over Zoom. As the date approaches, you will receive an email with the Zoom link.

About the Presenters

Julia Strayer, CPWA®, CIMA®, CRPC® Senior Vice President, Wealth Management Advisor.  Prior to joining Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2000, Julia was a vice president and private banker for BankBoston’s Private Bank for 7 years, responsible for asset management and trust services. Previously, Julia worked in marketing for 9 years with Merrill. Julia has a BA from Ohio State University and an MBA from New York University’s Stern School of Business. Julia has appeared on the CNBC show “Power Lunch,” CBS “This Morning,” WGCH’s “Women in Business,” in addition to featured articles in USA Today.

Liz Maccarone, CRPC® Senior Financial Advisor.  Liz joined Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2012. Liz works closely with high-net-worth individuals and their families to create personalized and comprehensive strategies that support their goals, including investment management, retirement planning, liability management, and multigenerational planning. Liz values the importance of establishing and cultivating relationships with families including the next generation. Liz graduated from Fairfield University with a dual bachelor’s degree in Finance and Marketing. She began her career working at a boutique investment firm as a Business Development Associate, specializing in commodities and futures trading.

title: Mystery Writers of America New York Chapter Panel - World-Building That Drives the Story and Creates Suspense
description:
Join us for a panel discussion by mystery authors as they reveal how they use words to build worlds. How do they set the scene for their novel that captivates readers, creates suspense on every page, and drives the story to a satisfying conclusion.

 

Panel and Bios:

Peggy Ehrhart is a former English professor with a doctorate in Medieval Literature. Her Maxx Maxwell mysteries, Sweet Man Is Gone (2008) and Got No Friend Anyhow (2011), were published by Five Star/Gale/Cengage and feature a blues-singer sleuth. More recently, Peggy has written the Knit & Nibble mysteries for Kensington Books. Book #12, Last Wool and Testament, was released in May, 2025; An Eggy Way to Die appeared in Kensington’s 2026 Easter novella anthology, Easter Egg Murder. In September Peggy will be launching a new cozy series with The Quilt Whisperer Investigates, also from Kensington. Peggy herself is an avid crafter, dating from her childhood as a member of the 4-H Club in rural Southern California. She now lives in Leonia, New Jersey.

Lori Robbins is the Amazon bestselling author of the On Pointe and Master Class mystery series, and a contributor to The Secret Ingredient: A Mystery Writers Cookbook. She is an Agatha Award nominee and the recipient of three Silver Falchions, the Indie Award for Best Mystery, and a silver medal in the Daphne du Maurier Award for Mystery and Suspense. Short stories include “Leading Ladies,” which received Honorable Mention in the 2022 Best American Mystery and Suspense anthology. After ten very lean years as a professional dancer, Lori became an English teacher and now writes full-time. Her experiences onstage, in the classroom, and at home, as the mother of six, have made her an expert in the homicidal tendencies everyday life inspires.

Valerie Wilson Wesley writes mysteries, novels and children’s books. Her latest book is The Mysterious Death of Junetta Plum, the first mystery of her Harriet Stone series. The Odessa Jones Mysteries include A Glimmer of Death (2021), A Fatal Glow (2022) and A Shimmer of Red (2023). She has also written nine mysteries in the popular Tamara Hayle Mystery series, including When Death Comes Stealing, named by Time magazine as one of the 100 best mysteries and thrillers. Her mysteries have been published in Germany, France and the UK. Wesley is a graduate of Howard University and holds master’s degrees from the Bank Street College of Education and the Columbia Graduate School of Journalism. She is a former executive editor of Essence magazine and a member of Crime Writers of Color, Sisters in Crime and Mystery Writers of America. https://valeriewilsonwesley.com

Yvonne Ventresca is an award-winning author with an MFA from Vermont College of Fine Arts. Her latest thriller, If I’m Gone, will be out in spring 2027 from Poisoned Pen Press. Told in a book-within-a-book narrative, it features a missing author who leaves behind a final manuscript that eerily mirrors her own life as a widow being stalked. Yvonne's previous work includes the YA novels Pandemic and Black Flowers, White Lies, as well as two nonfiction books and nine short stories. She serves on the Mystery Writers of America NY board and mentors through AWP and MWA. You can learn more at her website YvonneVentresca.com where she blogs aboutwriting productivity and features writing resources.

 

Part of Summer Reading 2026, Unearth a Story.

title: Let's Talk About Formula One NEW
location: Montclair Main - Classroom, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Formula 1 represents the pinnacle of auto racing. It emerged from the tradition of the Grand Prix in the early 20th century but the sport as we know it started after World War II, with open-wheeled cars, teams, drivers and sponsors of the highest caliber competing on road-courses around the globe. Today Formula 1 is experiencing unprecedented global growth, shifting from a niche motorsport into a mass entertainment juggernaut. 

We’ll talk about the history and evolution of the sport and how the present-day players have transformed it and continue to shape it. Where do you hope to see Formula 1 in 20 years? Will the classic race-courses survive? Will the diversity of design, race-courses and drivers flourish? Or will it just become another packaged entertainment spectacle? Come prepared to share your own ideas!

title: Simple Sitting Meditation
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**

I understand that this release discharges the SMC from any liability or claim that I, my heirs, or any personal representatives, may have against the SMC with respect to any bodily injury, illness, death, medical treatment, or property damage that may arise from, or in connection to, any SMC program. This liability waiver and release extends to the SMC along with Essex County and its staff and any other affiliated organization or SMC partner. **BY REGISTERING FOR THIS HIKE I attest I am in good health and attest that I: Am not experiencing any symptoms of illness such as cough, shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, fever, chills, repeated shaking with chills, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, or new loss of taste or smell.**
**Am following all CDC recommended guidelines, above, and limiting my exposure to the novel coronavirus/COVID-19.**
\# Arrival\, Weather\, & Cancellations
Please come to the starting point 10 minutes ahead of time so the hike can start promptly. Times are our best estimates; they can vary depending on conditions, and the size and pace of a group. If you have any questions, call the leader. **Temperatures above 90 degrees and steady rain cancels, but intermittent drizzle does not. You will *not* be notified.** **Bring water. Wear hiking boots, preferably waterproof with good soles and traction devices and bring poles (optional).** Dogs are not allowed on hikes unless specified.
These hikes are publicized first to SMC members and then advertised to the public one week before a hike. There is a limit of 25 participants, so pre-registration is required at least two days before a hike to sign the liability waiver online and allow lists to be sent to hike leaders. If you have registered and then find you cannot attend, please cancel your order online. **Repeated no shows without prior cancellation will result in removal from list.**

title: Architectural Walking Tour of Yale and Lunch in New Haven NEW
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Register by July 10. No refunds. Let's explore the world-famous architecture of Yale University and the quaint college town of New Haven!

GUIDE: Laszlo Kiss, an internationally known architect and popular Adult School instructor.

SCHEDULE:


	7 a.m. Leave Montclair
	10 a.m. Arrive New Haven
	10 a.m. - 12:30 P.M. Laszlo will lead us through a tour of Yale's modernist masterpieces by architects such as Louis Kahn, Eero Saarinen, Paul Rudolph, and Gordon Bunshaft of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill. We’ll also get to view great works of art inside the Yale Center for British Art and the Yale University Art Gallery.
	12:30-2 p.m. Lunch break. 
	
		Eat lunch on your own at one of the many cute campus-area eateries (including the famous Sally's Apizza) and browse the charming little shops, bookstores and coffeehouses near campus. 
		OR Join Laszlo for a 15-minute walk (each way) to the Ingalls Rink, Yale's modernist hockey arena. You'll still have time to catch a quick bite to eat.
	
	
	2:30 p.m.-3:30 p.m. Meet at Yale Visitors Center for student-led tour of the old campus, established in 1701, which is not accessible to solo visitors. This includes the iconic Gothic-style Sterling Memorial Library and the ivy-clad residential campuses.
	3:30-4 p.m.  Browse the Yale University Bookstore before getting back on the bus
	4:30 p.m. Board the bus for Montclair!


BRING:  Sunscreen, comfortable walking shoes, hat. Dress in layers. 

ACCESSIBILITY INFORMATION: This is a three-hour walking tour with some uneven ground. Some buildings do not include elevators. 

Please note: Lunch is not included. This trip will be held rain or shine.

title: Introduction to Wheel Throwing Pottery NEW
description:
Note: This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Discover the art of working on the potter’s wheel in this hands-on 6-week introductory course. Whether you're a complete beginner or looking to refine basic skills, this class offers a welcoming environment to explore the fundamentals of working with clay on the wheel.

You’ll learn the essential techniques of centering, pulling, shaping, and trimming clay to create functional forms like bowls and cups. As the course progresses, you’ll be introduced to glazing methods and the firing process, transforming your pieces into finished, food-safe ceramics. By the end of the session, you’ll have several unique, handmade pieces to take home and enjoy.

All clay, glaze, firings and tools are included.

For the first class, bring an apron or work clothes, sketchbook, writing implement and your curiosity!

title: MCP Server with Fabric (Power BI and data agents)
description:
Cloud Data Driven
In this session, I explore how the Model Context Protocol (MCP) enables a new way for AI agents to securely and intelligently interact with Microsoft Fabric.

You’ll see how MCP servers expose Power BI semantic models and Fabric data agents as discoverable tools, allowing agents to reason over enterprise data, query it in natural language, act on top of it and edit semantic models for Power BI.

I will walk through real scenarios where data agents and Power BI models become first-class citizens in agent workflows, unlocking more contextual, trustworthy, and scalable AI experiences across the Fabric ecosystem.

title: Help Desk - Bring Your Laptop, Yourself, and Your WordPress Problems
description:
WordPress Montclair Meetup
If you are running a WordPress site and are having issues and would like some help, then this Meetup is for you!

If you know some things, expert or not, and want to give back to the WordPress community, then this Meetup is for you too!

We will do our best to match a problem with a problem-solver. On-site and in real-time. Just bring yourself, your laptop, and your WordPress problems.

It's OK if you attend and only want to observe. We recognize this is how people learn. Given our time limit of two hours, we may not be able to solve everyone's issues, but we will try! If you are seeking help, please come prepared. Have your web site loaded in a browser, have your WordPress admin ready, along with a short list of issues you are trying to solve.

People helping are volunteers and may not be experts. There is risk to breaking your site! Please do not bring client or business sites that can impact reputations or revenue. If you have a staging site we can test things with, that is always preferred. If it is a production site, please create a site backup before having someone do any work on your site.

If you cannot find the group, please ask the front desk where the WordPress meetup group is meeting.

**PARKING**:
We've been asked to not park in the United Way lot behind the library as it could result in a parking ticket. Please find street parking or a parking deck.

\-\-\-
Join the **JerseyPress Slack** group to chat with others in our community and get help: [https://jerseypress.org/slack/](https://jerseypress.org/slack/)

title: Simple Sitting Meditation
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

description:

Pollinator Meadow activities will focus on pathway installation and invasive species sweep and removal. Work is strenuous to moderate. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can start promptly at 10 am.

Please dress appropriately! Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots. please no bug spray. Wear sunscreen and a hat. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

title: Simple Sitting Meditation
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Native Vector Search in SQL Server 2025: Building AI-Ready Applications
description:
Cloud Data Driven
SQL Server 2025 extends the data platform with native vector search, enabling AI-powered similarity queries directly inside the database. New vector data types and built-in index structures allow efficient storage and querying of high-dimensional embeddings (e.g., from NLP or image models). With optimized Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) algorithms and vector indexes, queries achieve millisecond-level response times - even across millions of vectors.

We will explore how vector indexes optimize performance by accelerating similarity searches and reducing resource consumption, while also discussing their limitations - such as index build times, storage overhead, and scenarios where approximate results may differ from exact matches.
Beyond the database engine, you will see how SQL Server 2025 integrates with Azure Foundry and Azure OpenAI Service, enabling embeddings generated by text and image models to be ingested directly into SQL via API calls. This allows developers to build end-to-end pipelines where model outputs are stored, indexed, and queried in real time - without external search infrastructure.

Use cases include real-time personalized recommendations, semantic analytics, and anomaly detection for security scenarios, all running on your proven SQL platform. Seamless integration with Azure hybrid scenarios enables vector search to scale across on-premises and cloud environments, while enterprise-grade features such as role-based access control and Always Encrypted ensure secure handling of sensitive embeddings.

By the end of this session, you will understand how to leverage SQL Server 2025’s native vector search, vector indexes, and AI integration to build scalable, secure, and intelligent applications - while being aware of their trade-offs and best practices for real-world deployments.

description:

JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - August meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**

title: Council On Ministries- Multi Platform
description: The UUCM Council on Ministries (CoM) exists to report to UUCM, its Board and Co-Ministers on how our programs are accomplishing their particular mission while also furthering the broader mission of UUCM. Special attention is paid to any systemic or cultural obstacles hindering our ability to fulfill our mission as well as any conflicts. Its primary goals are to maintain UUCM's Mission & Vision, restore trust and relationship when frayed, and to keep all our interactions in line with UUCM's covenant. Best practices, connectivity, cross-pollination and successes are also reported. The CoM also provides assistance evaluating our ministries periodically at the discretion of the Board. Please welcome Council on Ministries liaisons into your meetings and planning when they request to observe your functioning; share with them also your minutes and other documents when requested. title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Pollinator Meadow Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Pollinator Meadow activities will focus on pathway installation and invasive species sweep and removal. Work is strenuous to moderate. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can start promptly at 10 am.

Please dress appropriately! Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots. please no bug spray. Wear sunscreen and a hat. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program coordinator Lori LaBorde at citizenscience@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

**Meet at the meadow after parking in Shady Nook Picnic Area.**

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.
source: Meetup: Board Game Night at Verona Inn

title: Council On Ministries- Multi Platform
description: The UUCM Council on Ministries (CoM) exists to report to UUCM, its Board and Co-Ministers on how our programs are accomplishing their particular mission while also furthering the broader mission of UUCM. Special attention is paid to any systemic or cultural obstacles hindering our ability to fulfill our mission as well as any conflicts. Its primary goals are to maintain UUCM's Mission & Vision, restore trust and relationship when frayed, and to keep all our interactions in line with UUCM's covenant. Best practices, connectivity, cross-pollination and successes are also reported. The CoM also provides assistance evaluating our ministries periodically at the discretion of the Board. Please welcome Council on Ministries liaisons into your meetings and planning when they request to observe your functioning; share with them also your minutes and other documents when requested. They are charged by the Board to help us have a broad view of our function as it relates to living out our mission and vision, so let us all assist them in this important 'meta-work.'For more informationRev Scott Sammler-Michael (he, him, his) is inviting you to a scheduled Zoom meeting.Join Zoom MeetingMeeting ID: 824 8437 7822 Passcode: UUCM──────────UUCM A is inviting you to a scheduled Zoom meeting.Join Zoom Meetinghttps://us06web.zoom.us/j/86413216696?pwd=F7KiAnT4zCeeXSSbhxAjfyAGwd1gu1.1Meeting ID: 864 1321 6696Passcode: UUCM---One tap mobile+13092053325,,86413216696#,,,,*830036# US+13126266799,,86413216696#,,,,*830036# US (Chicago)Join instructionshttps://us06web.zoom.us/meetings/86413216696/invitations?signature=v3hMfWUIYPLp-gWs24aLluRKw8IaBywLV7XSaRjkSbo──────────

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

description:
Join NEEC for a festive evening celebrating another year
of community, sustainability, and bountiful harvests.

We are excited to invite community organizations, businesses, and individuals to become sponsors. For more information about sponsorship opportunities, email Amanda at amccabe@neearth.org.
